questions.q: Cresenciano de Castro is famously known for designing the original headquarters of which international financial institution located along Roxas Boulevard?
o: The Central Bank of the Philippines
questions.n: De Castro's design for the original ADB building (now the DFA) was a landmark of 1960s modernism in the Philippines.

questions.q: Which educational institution's main campus in Diliman features De Castro's distinctive Brutalist design, characterized by its interconnected concrete blocks?
questions.n: De Castro designed the iconic campus, using raw concrete and functional geometry to create a modern learning environment for the country's top scholars.

questions.q: De Castro designed the 'Philippine Atomic Energy Commission' building. What is the unique architectural shape of the nuclear reactor housing within this complex?
o: A concrete igloo or dome-like structure
questions.n: The 'PRR-1' reactor building is an iconic piece of scientific architecture that uses mass and form to convey its specialized function.

questions.q: De Castro's work is often categorized under 'Brutalism.' What is a primary material characteristic of this architectural movement?
o: Extensive use of polished gold and marble
questions.n: The term comes from the French for 'raw concrete,' celebrating the honest expression of the material and its texture.

questions.q: True or False: Cresenciano de Castro was the first Filipino architect to use a computerized system for architectural specifications and billing.
questions.n: He was a pioneer in integrating modern technology and efficient business practices into the Philippine architectural profession.
